provisions.title: H.J. Res. 78
provisions.heading: Congressional disapproval of the identified U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service longfin smelt rule
provisions.quote: That Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the United States Fish and Wildlife Service relating to Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for the San Francisco Bay-Delta Distinct Population Segment of the Longfin Smelt (89 Fed. Reg. 61029; published July 30, 2024), and such rule shall have no force or effect.
provisions.context:
H.J. Res. 78 invokes chapter 8 of title 5 and identifies one U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service rule by title, Federal Register citation, and publication date. Mr. LaMalfa submitted the analyzed introduced-in-House version on March 21, 2025, and it was referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources. Congress.gov separately records that the House passed the resolution 216–195 on May 1, 2025, and that the Senate received it on May 5, 2025. Its sole operative clause states that Congress disapproves the cited rule and that the rule shall have no force or effect; because the official status remains Passed House rather than enacted, that legal consequence remains contingent on enactment.

Source limits / honesty note: The cited rule is not reproduced, and the resolution supplies no findings, substantive replacement rule, implementation steps, quantitative target, reporting requirement, or downstream outcome. The source therefore supports only the express legal objective and enactment-contingent legal effect recorded below. It does not support a biological, water-management, agricultural, economic, or administrative outcome claim. The binary legal consequence is not a recurring empirical series, so this provision honestly has no forecastable metrics, series hints, stance matrices, or conditionals.
goals: Disapprove the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service rule cited at 89 Fed. Reg. 61029 so that it has no force or effect.

effects.mechanism: Direct legal effect — conditional on enactment
effects.text: If enacted, the resolution would disapprove the identified U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service rule and provide that it has no force or effect; the text does not state what regulatory status would replace it or identify any downstream outcome.
